links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of RFF Index versus age for composite outcome in rib fracture patients
links.effect: RFF had higher discrimination (OR 0.09, 95% CI 0.08-0.11 vs OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.04-0.08; p=0.04) and better calibration than age, though only in lower injury burden patients.
links.quote: The RFF score had higher discrimination (OR, 0.09; 95% CI, 0.08-0.11 vs. OR, 0.06; 95% CI, 0.04-0.08; p = 0.04) and calibration performance compared with age, but on secondary analysis, higher predictive performance was limited to patients with lower injury burden.

links.outcome: RFF Index performance across lower versus higher Injury Severity Score subgroups
links.effect: Higher predictive performance over age was limited to patients with lower injury burden (ISS <15); both models had poor calibration for discharge home after hospitalization >=5 days.
links.quote: The RFF score had higher discrimination (OR, 0.09; 95% CI, 0.08-0.11 vs. OR, 0.06; 95% CI, 0.04-0.08; p = 0.04) and calibration performance compared with age, but on secondary analysis, higher predictive performance was limited to patients with lower injury burden.

screen.reason: Prospective multicenter external validation of a machine learning-based risk score (Rib Fracture Frailty Index) compared against age; does not test an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
